疲倦.notes: Ordinary physical tiredness that wants rest: 感到疲倦 · 疲倦的眼神/神情 · 毫无疲倦之意 · 不知疲倦 tireless. Milder than 疲惫 (worn out) and more written than 累. 疲劳 is fatigue as a measurable state. Mnemo: 疲 = 疒 (illness) + 皮 (skin) — worn thin; 倦 = 亻 (person) + 卷 (roll up) — a person rolled up, done for the day.
疲倦.sentence: 孩子玩了一天，脸上带着疲倦的神情。
疲倦.pinyin: Háizi wán le yì tiān, liǎn shàng dàizhe píjuàn de shénqíng.
疲倦.english: The child played all day, and wore a tired look on his face.

疲劳.notes: Fatigue as a measurable state, and the technical term: 消除疲劳 · 疲劳驾驶 driving while tired · 视觉疲劳 · 金属疲劳 metal fatigue. It works as a noun, where 疲倦 and 疲惫 stay adjectives. 疲倦 is simply tired; 疲惫 is worn out. Mnemo: 疲 (worn thin) + 劳 (labour) — what the work leaves behind.

疲惫.notes: The strong one — worn out, not merely tired: 疲惫不堪 · 身心疲惫 · 一脸疲惫 · 疲惫的身影. Written register. 疲倦 is ordinary tiredness, 疲劳 is fatigue as a state, and 累 is the everyday spoken word. Mnemo: 惫 = 备 (prepare) over 心 (heart) — the heart has nothing left in reserve.

厌倦.notes: Not physical tiredness at all — fed up WITH something: 对…感到厌倦 · 厌倦了这种生活 · 令人厌倦. It takes an object or 对…, while 疲倦 describes the body and takes none. Sharing 倦 with 疲倦 is the trap. Mnemo: 厌 (loathe) + 倦 (weary) — weary to the point of loathing.
